newsitem.title: ITALY: UN agency hopes to begin Zaire airlift during day.
newsitem.headline: UN agency hopes to begin Zaire airlift during day.

text.p: The U.N.'s World Food Programme said on Wednesday it hoped to begin an emergency airlift of relief supplies to eastern Zaire during the day.
"The airlift will begin as soon as the Zairean authorities give us the green light, which we hope will be within the day," chief spokesman Trevor Rowe said in a statement.
He said the airlift would begin with a Hercules C-130 plane now in Kampala and would increase according to needs.
"Our intention is to establish an emergency stockpile of food and emergency relief items in Goma which we can use depending on needs," Rowe said.
The agency is currently distributing food to the estimated 727,000 refugees in the Goma area in eastern Zaire, where it estimates current food needs at 300 tonnes per day.
More than a week of fighting has driven some half a million Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees out of camps in east Zaire.
In Geneva, European donors and Western aid agencies reacting to the worsening crisis in eastern Zaire have ended inconclusive talks, diplomats said on Wednesday.
Diplomats said the closed-door meeting called on French initiative ended late on Tuesday with no decisions taken on how to help the refugees.
"It was a very inconclusive meeting. It was a brainstorming session and didn't lead to any concrete suggestions," said one diplomat.
"As long as there is no ceasefire agreement, it is impossible to provide humanitarian aid in the area," he added.
Officials from the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR and the WFP were also present at the crisis talks.
